Which OpenAPI generator should you trust for rapid iteration? A recent DEV Community roundup tested four popular tools on a synthetic spec with 1,200 operations and 484 schemas, using a Ryzen 9 7900 under Node 26.

Kubb v5 generated types in a median of 337 ms, the fastest among the group, while Hey API reduced its SDK generation time to 1,329 ms, an 82 % improvement over six months ago. Openapi‑typescript sat at 438 ms, and Orval took 866 ms for type‑only generation.

Memory usage also differed: Kubb peaked at 156 MiB, openapi‑typescript at 191 MiB, Hey API at 240 MiB, and Orval at 145 MiB. Generated file counts ranged from a single 1.45 MB file for openapi‑typescript to 2,897 files totaling 3.13 MB for Kubb.

"Generation speed directly shapes how quickly we can iterate on an API contract."

These differences matter because faster generation shortens feedback loops and lower memory footprints keep CI runners stable, especially on shared environments with limited resources.

The benchmarks reflect a single hardware setup and synthetic spec, so results may vary with real‑world APIs.

Which generator’s trade‑offs align best with your team’s workflow and CI constraints?
